text: - **Highlights**: signed-in users select text → "Highlight" pill → publishes a NIP-84 (`kind:9802`) event tagged to the essay's canonical URL, wrapped locally right away (optimistic, doesn't wait on relay confirmation). [...] - **Highlights**: NIP-84 (`kind:9802`), content = selected text, `r` tag = canonical URL, `context` tag = surrounding paragraph. Select text → "Highlight" button → publish. [...] - **Reading**: on load, subscribes for existing highlights on that URL from four public relays and marks up matching text in place, with a hover tooltip showing who highlighted it and when. [...] Assistant: **Fixed and verified.** The bug you hit — clicking "Highlight" doing nothing, not even prompting a signature — was a real DOM race: the global `mouseup` listener that opens the toolbar wasn't ignoring mouseup events that landed on the toolbar itself, so clicking it destroyed-and-recreated the button mid-click, which silently suppresses the browser's `click` event on the now-detached original element. Added a guard (`f7z.io/src/highlights.js`) so the listener ignores mouseup events originating inside `.n-hl-toolbar`, rebuilt `js/highlights.js`, and re-ran the full flow in a real browser with a fake NIP-07 provider: sign-in → select text → click Highlight → `<mark class="n-highlight">` appears wrapping the selection → hover tooltip shows the highlighter's name/npub and timestamp. All confirmed working.
